clauses.reason: The approval clause says the President does "do order that the said Code of Fair Competition be and it is hereby approved". That is a section 3(a) approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Pleating, Stitching and Bonnaz and Hand Embroidery Industry, conditioned as the next two clauses state, with no stated period for the approval itself. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113) repealed the provisions of Title I delegating power to the President to "approve or prescribe codes of fair competition" and "providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed"; the resolution states no effective date other than its approval ("Approved, June 14, 1935."), so the approval stopped operating on June 14, 1935. Under section 3 of Title I (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA3) an approved code had legal effect only through 3(b) standards of fair competition, 3(c) injunctions and 3(f) misdemeanor penalties, all of which the repeal removed. Schechter (SUPPLEMENT:SCHECHTERJDG, May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date, and June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936.

The condition provides that "the Code Authority shall report to the Administrator thereon, within sixty (60) days after the effective date hereof, with recommendations for the continuation, elimination or modification of any or all of the wage rates provided in the Code", and that "Upon the approval of the Administrator, after such notice and hearing as he may prescribe, the aforesaid recommendations or any of them, shall become effective provisions of the Code". It is a condition of the approval (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA3, section 3(a)); the report period is a deadline measured from an effective date no held source states, and a deadline is not an end. No held record shows the study, the report or any approved recommendation, so no performance date is claimed. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113) repealed the provisions of Title I delegating power to the President to "approve or prescribe codes of fair competition" and "providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed"; the resolution states no effective date other than its approval ("Approved, June 14, 1935."), so the approval stopped operating on June 14, 1935. Under section 3 of Title I (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA3) an approved code had legal effect only through 3(b) standards of fair competition, 3(c) injunctions and 3(f) misdemeanor penalties, all of which the repeal removed. Schechter (SUPPLEMENT:SCHECHTERJDG, May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date, and June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. The condition and the recommendations it could make effective operated only as provisions of the approved code and stopped with the approval on June 14, 1935.

The proviso reserves that "the Administrator may at any time after the effective date of the Code, cause hearings to be held for the purpose of determining whether the wage rates provided in the Code are in fact tending to establish maximum wages". It is a standing power over the code's wage rates with no stated end of its own, exercisable only while the code was approved. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113) repealed the provisions of Title I delegating power to the President to "approve or prescribe codes of fair competition" and "providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed"; the resolution states no effective date other than its approval ("Approved, June 14, 1935."), so the approval stopped operating on June 14, 1935. Under section 3 of Title I (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA3) an approved code had legal effect only through 3(b) standards of fair competition, 3(c) injunctions and 3(f) misdemeanor penalties, all of which the repeal removed. Schechter (SUPPLEMENT:SCHECHTERJDG, May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date, and June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. No held record shows any hearing under the proviso.

The condition directing the Code Authority to study and report on wage rates and providing for the Administrator's approval of recommendations.

Identity and page check: the held text for EO 6598 is the American Presidency Project transcription (APP node 362355), registered as grade mirror_transcription (not an original). Its page record is a Common Crawl capture of 2026-01-17T19:02:31Z whose heading names Executive Order 6598, whose date (February 10, 1934) and subject agree with the text, and whose text sha256 equals the held text's. The WPA 1944 list row (1934 Feb 10 p.567: Code of Fair Competition for the Pleating,Stitchingand Bonnaz and Hand Embroidery Industry conditionallyapproved. VI NRA Codes 403.) confirms the order's date and subject. The order approves a code of fair competition under section 3(a) of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, so the reviewed shared analysis (SHARED_ANALYSIS.md and review-shared/ADJUDICATION.json) applies: a code-dependent command that did not end earlier ended on June 14, 1935 by statutory repeal (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2); Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date. The machine inventory had one clause covering the approval, the study-and-report condition and the proviso; it is corrected into three clauses so each command has its own end. The WPA row calls the approval conditional.

savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the approved Code of Fair Competition for the Pleating, Stitching and Bonnaz and Hand Embroidery Industry before June 14, 1935 are accrued consequences that the repeal did not turn into continuing commands; nothing in S.J. Res. 113 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113) continues the approval after June 14, 1935. Any antitrust exemption for complying action before the repeal (NIRA section 5, SUPPLEMENT:NIRA5) is likewise an accrued effect; the resolution's proviso, which extends the exemption only to "agreements and action thereunder" meeting stated conditions, leaves open how far it narrowed the exemption for past action, so the claim records no continuing exemption and no surviving approval. Any study made, report filed or recommendation made effective before the repeal is an accrued act, not a continuing command.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date
source_notes.reason: A. L. A. Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, 295 U.S. 495, decided May 27, 1935: the Court held the section 3 code-making delegation unconstitutional and the Live Poultry Code provisions in question invalid. Recorded as a validity characterization for every section 3 code approval, not as this order's end; the judgment did not cancel or withdraw this order.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1933-06-16: enactment date of NIRA section 3; the provisions described were repealed on June 14, 1935 (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2).
source_notes.reason: NIRA section 3 (48 Stat. 195, June 16, 1933): under 3(a) the President approved codes and could impose conditions of approval; under 3(b), 3(c) and 3(f) an approved code's provisions became standards of fair competition enforceable by injunction and as misdemeanors. These are the legal effects that section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1933-06-16: enactment date of NIRA section 5; S.J. Res. 113 (June 14, 1935) limited the exemption by proviso; the held text does not settle the proviso's effect on past action.
source_notes.reason: NIRA section 5 exempted from the antitrust laws any code approved and in effect under Title I and any complying action while Title I was in effect and for sixty days thereafter; any exemption for action taken before the repeal is an accrued effect, not continued operation of the approval.
